---
title: "How do I test for a linear association between two numerical variables?"
---

## What the question asks

How do I test for a linear association between two numerical variables?

## Steps in RStudio

1. Check x and y are paired and numerical.

2. Plot them for curves and outliers.

3. Run cor.test(x,y) and report r, its interval, and p-value separately.

## Runnable example

```{r}
x <- c(2,4,5,7,8,10,11,13)
y <- c(3,5,6,9,8,12,11,15)
plot(x,y,pch=19,col="#3F78A8",xlab="X",ylab="Y")
result <- cor.test(x,y,method="pearson")
print(result$estimate)
print(result$conf.int)
print(result$p.value)
```

## Interpret the result

Pearson's r summarizes linear association, while the p-value addresses a null hypothesis under assumptions. Neither proves causation.

## Check before using real data

Outliers, curved patterns, dependence, and restricted measurement ranges can invalidate a simple interpretation.
